title: public-trust-layer
universal_lens: The Public Trust Layer formalizes epistemic transparency as a constrained projection operator. It maps high-dimensional, noisy intelligence states onto a low-dimensional public manifold, strictly enforcing source-tier filtration and calibrated confidence bounds to minimize information asymmetry and prevent stochastic tout-like degeneracy.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the trust layer acts as a conformal prediction filter. Confidence scores are dynamically recalibrated against settled outcomes (N≥30), ensuring predictive intervals maintain strict coverage probabilities. Unverified signals remain in latent Tier 5 spaces, explicitly excluded from public posterior distributions.
gse_mapping: For GSE, this doctrine dictates state-transition rules for user-facing outputs. The system transitions from raw signal ingestion to public commitment only when explicit tier thresholds are met, actively vetoing any state rendering 'locks' or unverified rumors as deterministic facts.

primitives.name: Epistemic Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Public Trust Layer governs what the platform publicly commits to, how it discloses its methods, and what language it uses when talking about itself.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: Projection operator (dimensionless); S: High-dimensional internal intelligence state; U: User-facing public commitment space.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if P becomes the identity operator (I), exposing raw, uncalibrated internal states directly to users, collapsing into a tout service.

primitives.name: Conformal Calibration Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: A confidence score of 72 means the model has a historical record consistent with 72 — it does not mean the pick will win 72% of the time.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C: Confidence score (dimensionless percentage); H: Historical settlement record (count); N: Number of settled picks (integer).
primitives.assumptions: Requires a minimum sample size (N ≥ 30) to establish statistical significance before C is published.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs at N < 30, where the empirical distribution is too sparse, forcing C to default to a capped baseline.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's conformal inference engine, where predicted risk scores are adjusted based on the nonconformity of new data points relative to a calibration set.
layer2.telemetry: Variance between stated confidence C and realized win-rate over rolling windows of 30+ picks.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T: Source tier integer (1-5); B: Boolean boundary condition for public display.
primitives.assumptions: Information hierarchy is strictly ordered; Tier 5 (rumors) possesses insufficient entropy reduction to cross the public boundary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the boundary condition B(T=5) evaluates to True, allowing noise to masquerade as signal in the public domain.

layer2.telemetry: Count of Tier 5 signals intercepted and prevented from reaching public surfaces per unit time.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Public Trust Layer operates as a rigorous mathematical constraint on information flow, preventing the collapse of a sophisticated intelligence network into a degenerate tout service. By defining a projection operator P, we map the vast, noisy internal state space S—comprising raw telemetry, unverified chatter, and preliminary model outputs—onto a highly restricted public manifold U. This projection is governed by two primary filters: the Conformal Calibration Kernel and the Tier Filtration Boundary.

The Conformal Calibration Kernel ensures that any scalar metric exposed to the user, such as a confidence score C, is strictly bound to empirical reality. It enforces a minimum sample size threshold (N ≥ 30) before allowing C to reflect a model's specific output, otherwise defaulting to a conservative baseline. This prevents overfitting narratives and aligns with Bayesian updating principles, where priors are heavily penalized until sufficient likelihood data is accumulated.

Simultaneously, the Tier Filtration Boundary acts as a hard potential barrier. Information possessing a Tier rating T ≥ 5 (rumors, unverified social chatter) is mathematically forbidden from crossing into U as a deterministic fact. While these signals may influence internal latent variables, their public representation is strictly limited to uncertainty-laden disclosures. The failure mode of this system is the relaxation of these boundaries—if P approaches the identity matrix or the Tier boundary lowers, the system loses its epistemic integrity, indistinguishable from standard market noise amplifiers.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits from Shannon’s information theory, specifically channel capacity and noise filtration, merged with modern conformal prediction methodologies introduced by Vovk et al. Historically, it reacts against the opaque 'black box' models of early quantitative finance, adopting instead the rigorous disclosure standards demanded by regulatory bodies like the SEC, translating legal compliance into algorithmic constraints. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The system models the user not merely as a consumer of picks, but as a rational agent requiring verifiable evidence chains to update their own priors. It anticipates adversarial actors (touts, manipulators) who exploit cognitive biases by overstating certainty. By explicitly disclosing weaknesses and capping unproven confidence, the Trust Layer builds a cooperative game-theoretic equilibrium where long-term credibility outweighs short-term click-through optimization.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent leakage, the Trust Layer maintains strict anti-collinearity with the internal Claim Governance module. While Claim Governance dictates what the system is allowed to compute internally, the Trust Layer dictates what can be rendered. A veto is triggered if an internal high-confidence state relies predominantly on Tier 5 inputs; the Trust Layer must override the output, suppressing the pick or downgrading its public tier regardless of internal algorithmic conviction.
